problem_text:
A logistics firm must devise a procurement and storage strategy for a critical fuel additive over a 14-day operational cycle.  
Initial stock at the start of the cycle is 62 gallons.  
On any day \( t = 1, \dots, 14 \), the supplier permits an order whose volume must be between 7 and 79 gallons.  
Each order, however, requires a lead time of 1 day before it becomes available to meet requirements or augment stock.  
Daily consumption of the additive is as follows:  

* Day 1: 10 gallons  
* Day 2: 17 gallons  
* Day 3: 33 gallons  
* Day 4: 56 gallons  
* Day 5: 40 gallons  
* Day 6: 30 gallons  
* Day 7: 16 gallons  
* Day 8: 53 gallons  
* Day 9: 38 gallons  
* Day 10: 33 gallons  
* Day 11: 47 gallons  
* Day 12: 54 gallons  
* Day 13: 26 gallons  
* Day 14: 52 gallons  

Shortfalls are tolerated, but any unsatisfied consumption is lost and not carried forward.  
Throughout the 14-day window, additive quantities may be treated as continuous, and the physical storage tank can hold at most 62 gallons at any moment.  
Total cost comprises three elements: a procurement cost of 5 per gallon ordered; a storage cost of 3 per gallon kept overnight; and a penalty of 7 per gallon of unmet daily consumption.  
The objective is to schedule optimal order quantities each day and monitor the consequent stock and shortage levels so as to minimize the aggregate expenditure.
